title: The Town of the Messengers
art: The messengers, the townspeople and the man who came running appear only as lights. His death is shown only as his light rising; Paradise is not depicted. That he was named Habib is from the commentaries (36:13–29).
The look of the town is imagined; its mud-brick walls and flat roofs are of the kind built in this people's time.
imagePrompt: A walled town at evening, three steady lights standing in the square before a jeering crowd of dim lights; one warm light running the length of the long street from the far edge of the town; then that light rising softly into the sky; then a single white flash and every light in the town gone out, the streets silent; ink-wash and parchment texture.

beats.say: The Quran tells of a town to which God sent two messengers, then a third to strengthen them. You are only men like us, the people said; we see an evil omen in you, and if you do not stop, we will stone you. Then a man came running from the far end of the town: my people, follow the messengers!
They killed him for his faith. Enter Paradise, he was told; and he said: if only my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me and honoured me.
After him, no army from heaven was needed: there was only one cry, and they were extinguished.

verse.en: And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers.
